Émile Zola, His Masterpiece, translated by Ernest Alfred Vizetelly.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/emile-zola/his-masterpiece/ernest-alfred-vizetelly

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- Émile Zola, the author, died 1902.
- Ernest Alfred Vizetelly, the translator, the annotator and the writer of the preface, died 1922.

First publication of the text used: 1902 (SE colophon: 'His Masterpiece was published in 1885 by Émile Zola. It was translated from French in 1902 by Ernest Alfred Vizetelly.')

Why this is public domain:
- United States: the Standard Ebooks rights statement says the text is in the US public domain, and the text was a translation first published in 1902, before 1931, so it is public domain there.
- Country of origin: every person named above died in 1925 or earlier, so the text is public domain in every country with a term of life + 100 years or less. The last to die did so in 1922, so this holds by 1 January 2023.

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."
